comments.body:
# RCA (rebar-debug Phase 1) — MEASURED: the verifier LOOPS; it does not converge at any budget

Reproduced at the default budget in an instrumented run (every agent tool call logged).
`verify_completion(e369, graph=False, source="attested", ref="HEAD")` — identical failure,
`max_iterations=480`, 1074s, **264 tool calls**.

## The measurement that settles the question

| | |
|---|---|
| tool calls to death | 264 (185 `search_files`, 67 `read_file`, 5 `show_ticket`, 5 `list_directory`) |
| distinct call signatures | **135** |
| novelty, calls 1-132 | **94-98% novel** (genuine exploration) |
| novelty, calls 133-198 | 12% novel |
| novelty, calls **199-264** | **0% novel** |
| loop entered | call **#121, t=537s** — 50% of wall clock, 55% of calls spent in the loop |

From call #121 the agent is in a **closed 4-call cycle**, repeated 31-37x, all against ONE file
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_characterization.py`:

    x37  search_files("deleted",   <that file>)     -> "(no matches)"
    x32  search_files("J1 oracle", <that file>)     -> "(no matches)"
    x31  search_files("J1",        <that file>)     -> "(no matches)"
    x31  read_file(<that file>, line_start=115, line_end=30)  -> 11,000 chars

**Verdict: it does NOT converge at any budget.** More budget buys more identical cycles. That
is why 1600 failed exactly like 480. Raising the floor again is proven futile.

**Genuine work needed: ~118 distinct tool calls** (the distinct-signature count before the loop).
The existing 480 floor is already ~3.5x adequate. **No budget increase is warranted.**

## Proven root cause: `search_files` silently lies when `path` names a FILE

`src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py:99-140`. The body is `for dirpath, dirs, files in os.walk(base)`;
`os.walk` on a FILE (or a nonexistent path) yields nothing, so control falls through to
`return "\n".join(hits) or "(no matches)"` (**pai_tools.py:140**). There is no file/dir
discrimination and no existence check.

Proven live, in-run, against ground truth:

* `search_files("J1", ".../test_backend_characterization.py")` -> `(no matches)` — **`J1` is on
  line 116 of that file.** This is the loop's engine: the agent is verifying the epic's AC #6
  ("characterization oracles pinning every unit"), it needs the `J1` oracle marker, and the
  tool denies it exists 31 times.
* `search_files("allow_insecure", "src/rebar/_config_schema.py")` -> `(no matches)` — **21 real
  hits.** (Evidence for AC #11.)
* `search_files("resolved_statuses", "src/rebar/_config_schema.py")` -> `(no matches)` (twice) —
  **5 real hits.** (AC #13.)
* `search_files("LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA", ".../jira/outbound_fields.py")` -> `(no matches)` —
  real hit on line 36. (AC #10.)
* `search_files("jira-datacenter", "tests/.../test_backend_contract.py")` -> `(no matches)` —
  1 real hit. (AC #2.)

Aggregate over the whole run: **48% of `search_files` calls passed a FILE path; 100% of those
returned `(no matches)`; 26 of 29 had the literal genuinely present** — i.e. **29% of every tool
call in the run was a guaranteed-false negative.**

This also makes it a **false-FAIL vector on a signed gate**: the `completion-verifier` prompt
tells the agent that `(no matches)` means "only that *that literal string* is absent" and to
establish absence by searching by symbol and listing the directory. Narrowing to the file — the
most natural move, and one the prompt encourages — returns a lie.

## Why the loop is fatal rather than self-correcting (4 compounding, each cited)

1. **No loop breaker.** No tool-call dedup anywhere in the agent loop. The shipped
   forced-landing primitive `RunRequest.tool_step_limit` (withdraw tools after N run steps,
   `src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py:64-75`) is **never set for the primary verify step** —
   `build_agent_request` does not set it (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py:327-338`) and the gate
   YAML cannot. Its only caller is bounded recovery
   (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:471`, `_EVIDENCE_TOOL_STEPS=16`).
2. **Greedy decoding removes the escape.** `temperature=0.0` is pinned for the verifier
   (`src/rebar/llm/completion.py:530-532`). Identical history -> identical next action. This is
   why the failure is *reproducible and budget-independent*, not flaky.
3. **The bounded recovery is UNREACHABLE for this failure mode.** Step-budget exhaustion raises
   `LLMRunnerError` (`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:95-103`). `CompletionAgentStep.run`
   catches ONLY `UnretryableOutputError` and only when `_is_token_exhaustion` holds
   (`completion_recovery.py:426-432`). Per `src/rebar/llm/errors.py:29-46`, `LLMRunnerError` is a
   strict *ancestor* of `UnretryableOutputError`, so it never matches.
   **Experiment E1 (run, with control):** a synthetic budget `LLMRunnerError` -> `RESULT:
   propagated`, `failure_diagnostic is None`; the control, a truncation `UnretryableOutputError`
   -> `RECOVERY-ENTERED`. The designed "narrow the task" machinery exists and is simply not wired
   to the failure that needs it.
4. **The diagnostic is computed and then dropped.** `interpret_failure` builds the repetition
   summary (`tool_calls_distinct`, `max_consecutive_repeat`, `top_repeated_tool_calls`) and
   attaches it as `budget_err.diagnostic` (`structured_run.py:79-101`). Because (3) leaves
   `failure_diagnostic is None`, `raise_completion_workflow_failure` skips `emit_gate_error`
   (`completion_recovery.py:382-403`) — **no `gate_error_v1` sidecar, diagnostic discarded**. In
   the instrumented run the propagated exception carried `DIAGNOSTIC: null`. That is exactly why
   the gate "cannot be tuned because it cannot be observed" — the signal exists and is thrown away
   one frame from the surface.

Then `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:293-297` appends `Override with --force-close="…"`
unconditionally, including to a pure **resource** exhaustion.

## Corrections to two assumptions in the report

* **Descendant count is NOT the LLM driver.** The verifier made only **5 `show_ticket` calls over
  5 distinct tickets** — it never walked the 59 descendants. `graph=False` is working as designed.
* **Child verdicts are not re-derived as tickets, but their proof is discarded.**
  `child_closure_findings(e369)` returns `blocking=0, uncertified=0` (measured) — deterministic
  proof that all children are closed AND certified. `gate_ops.py:132` collapses that to a single
  boolean routed to `reconcile`; **nothing about it reaches the verifier's prompt**
  (`completion-verification.yaml:48-56` wires only `context`). So the epic's AC #1 ("every child
  story is closed and its change is Verified +1") is handed to the LLM with zero evidence, and its
  Gerrit half is not obtainable from the repo at all.
* **Descendant count DOES drive a deterministic cost:** `child_closure_findings` 47.5s +
  `epic_bug_floor_findings` 41.0s = **88s of pure CPU before any LLM call**. Not the failure, but
  it does scale with subtree size, contrary to `docs/llm-framework.md:680-683`.

## Legitimacy: `defect`

Authoritative sources violated:
* `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md` — the tool contract it states to the agent
  ("a `(no matches)` result means only that *that literal string* is absent") is false.
* `docs/llm-framework.md:698-704` — "a high recursion limit means *you're paying for a loop, fix
  the loop*". The gate's own message advises the opposite (`Raise REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS`).
* `docs/llm-framework.md:720+` — bounded recovery is the documented answer to an exhausted
  aggregate call; it is unreachable here.

## Fix shape, sized to the evidence (no budget change)

1. **`search_files` must handle a file path and a missing path** — `pai_tools.py:99-140`: scan the
   single file when `base` is a file; return an explicit `Error: no such path …` when it does not
   exist, never `(no matches)`. ~5 lines. Removes the loop's fuel and closes a signed-gate
   false-FAIL vector. Same latent issue in `read_file` (`pai_tools.py:63`: an inverted range
   `line_end < line_start` silently becomes read-to-EOF rather than an error).
2. **Set `tool_step_limit` on the primary verify step** (`runs.py:327-338`, primitive at
   `agent_call.py:64-75`) so the run *lands with a verdict* instead of being killed empty —
   a structural loop breaker independent of any single tool bug.
3. **Route the budget `LLMRunnerError` into the existing bounded recovery**
   (`completion_recovery.py:426-432`). It fits this epic: 14 criteria <= `_MAX_CRITERIA` 32, and
   the context is 99,347 chars vs the 100,000 cap — **653 chars of headroom**, itself a fragility.
4. **Set `failure_diagnostic` from `exc.diagnostic` on the budget path** so the `gate_error_v1`
   sidecar is written and the operator message carries `tool_calls / distinct /
   max_consecutive_repeat`.
5. **Stop offering `--force-close` for a resource exhaustion** (`close_precheck.py:293-297`).

## Can e369 be closed honestly today, without `--force-close`?

**No.** Raising the budget is proven futile (0% novelty at death). `--ref <sha>` retargets the
tree, not the criteria set. The standalone `verify-completion` runs the same verifier. The one
mechanism that would work — bounded per-criterion recovery, which starts each criterion in a
fresh history (so the loop cannot persist) and withdraws tools at step 16 — is unreachable
(item 3). **Fix (1) is the smallest change that plausibly lets e369 close honestly.**

Evidence trace preserved at `/tmp/bf31-trace-evidence.jsonl` (264 rows).

## CORRECTION to this ticket's own framing — two of my assumptions are REFUTED by the Phase 1 evidence

I filed this ticket. The RCA comment above supersedes it on three points; recording the correction
here so the description is not read as current.

**1. 'The gate does not scale to a 59-descendant epic' — REFUTED as the LLM driver.** The verifier
made only **5 `show_ticket` calls over 5 distinct tickets**; it never walked the 59 descendants.
`graph=False` works as designed. Descendant count DOES drive ~88s of deterministic pre-LLM CPU
(`child_closure_findings` 47.5s + `epic_bug_floor_findings` 41.0s), which contradicts
`docs/llm-framework.md:680-683`, but that is not what exhausts the step budget.

**2. 'Two exhaustions suggest non-convergence' — CONFIRMED, and upgraded from inference to
measurement.** 264 tool calls; novelty 94-98% for calls 1-132, 12% for 133-198, **0% for 199-264**;
loop entered at call #121 (50% of wall clock). A closed 4-call cycle repeated 31-37x against ONE file.

**3. 'Raise the budget' — proven FUTILE, and my two attempts (480, then 1600) were wasted spend.**
Genuine work needs ~118 distinct calls, so the existing 480 floor is already ~3.5x adequate. I
escalated a budget when the correct read was that a budget was never the constraint.

### The actual cause, and why it is much bigger than this epic

`llm/pai_tools.py:99-140` — `search_files` returns `(no matches)` when `path` names a FILE, because
`os.walk` on a file yields nothing and control falls through to the empty-result return. Measured in
one run: **48% of `search_files` calls passed a file path; 100% of those returned `(no matches)`;
26 of 29 had the literal genuinely present.** `search_files('J1', …test_backend_characterization.py)`
returned `(no matches)` while `J1` sits on line 116.

**This is a false-FAIL vector on a SIGNED gate**, not merely a loop: the completion-verifier prompt
tells the agent `(no matches)` means the literal is absent, and encourages narrowing the path — which
is precisely the call that lies. Any prior verdict that turned on a narrowed `search_files` is
suspect.

### What stands from the original framing

The **trap** stands and is now better evidenced: `close_precheck.py:293-297` appends
`Override with --force-close="…"` unconditionally to what is a pure RESOURCE failure, while the
bounded recovery that would have produced an honest verdict is unreachable (`LLMRunnerError` is a
strict ancestor of the caught types) and the computed diagnostic is dropped one frame from the
surface. So the gate offers the forbidden exit as its only reachable one, and simultaneously discards
the signal that would let anyone tune it.

# Phase 2 (Repair) — scoped to the `search_files` path defect

Gerrit change **1433** — `bf31: search_files must not fake "(no matches)"`
https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1433

## Files in the diff (2)

* `src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py` (+43 −19)
* `tests/unit/test_pai_tools_search_files_bf31.py` (new, 10 cases)

## RED evidence (before any fix existed)

    pytest tests/unit/test_pai_tools_search_files_bf31.py -q
    -> 6 failed, 3 passed        (exit 1)

The 6 failures are the three file-path-with-hit cases and the three nonexistent-path cases; each
fails on the specific assertion that `"(no matches)"` was returned for a literal that is present, or
for a path that cannot be searched. The **3 that passed pre-fix are the ones that must not regress**
— honest absence, the directory branch, and root confinement — so the oracle is not merely failing
everywhere.

## Held-out discipline

The test file was **moved out of the fixer's working tree** (`/tmp/bf31-heldout/`) before the
implementation subagent was launched, and the subagent was given only the confirmed mechanism, the
reproduction, and a prose contract card — never the fixture, assertions, or path. It was told not to
create or look for tests. GREEN was verified by re-applying the held-out oracle afterwards:

    pytest tests/unit/test_pai_tools_search_files_bf31.py -q  ->  10 passed  (exit 0)

## Mutation checks (both required, both performed)

1. **Re-introduced the exact root cause** — deleted the file/missing-path discrimination so
   `os.walk` silently yields nothing again: **6 failed (exit 1)**; restoring the fix: 10 passed
   (exit 0). The oracle has teeth against the original defect.
2. **Applied the discovery filter to the file branch** (the subtle re-introduction the plan review's
   G6 finding predicted): **1 failed (exit 1)**; restored: 10 passed (exit 0).

Mutation 2 mattered. My **first** version of that test was vacuous — its `tmp_path` root was not a
git repo, so `_git_tracked` returned `None`, `skip_file` never fired, and the assertion could not
fail. The mutation check exposed it (`MUTATION2_EXIT=0`), and the case was rewritten with a real git
repo, a `.gitignore`d file, and an explicit pre-assertion that the filter is genuinely armed before
the real assertion is trusted. An assertion that cannot fail is not evidence.

## Gates (real exit codes)

| gate | exit |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/unit/test_pai_tools_search_files_bf31.py -q` | 0 (10 passed) |
| `make lint` | 0 |
| `make typecheck` | 0 (mypy, 435 files) |
| `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 4 --dist worksteal -q` | 1 — **1 pre-existing failure**, 10440 passed, 46 skipped |

The single CI failure is `tests/unit/grounding/test_coverage_reconstruction.py::test_full_backend_account_is_present`.
Verified pre-existing: re-run with this change **stashed**, on a clean tree at `origin/main`
`68ae305cef`, it still fails identically (exit 1). Filed as [rebar:354d-c85d-6689-4302].

## Fix-safety audit

* **Restoration, not creation** — no new entry point, command or user-visible artifact; two cases
  that returned a false `"(no matches)"` now return a true hit list and an explicit error.
* **No new dependency** — `os` only, already imported.
* **No test weakened** — no pre-existing test was touched (`git diff --stat` = 2 files, one new).
* **Directory branch held** — the caller-dependency sweep found every gate reaches this tool through
  the directory branch, which is byte-identical (shared `scan_one` helper preserves the hit format
  and both caps) and now pinned by a regression test.

## Step 7 sweep

* **Construct axis** — swept every `os.walk(` in `src/rebar` (8 sites). The other 7 take
  internally-derived roots (snapshot dirs, `repo_root`, cache paths), never an agent-supplied path.
  No siblings.
* **Parity axis** — rule: *a read-only agent tool must not report an unsearchable path as an honest
  empty result*. Census, each probed live: `list_directory(FILE)` -> `Error: Not a directory` OK;
  `list_directory(MISSING)` -> `Error` OK; `read_file(DIRECTORY)` -> `Error: Is a directory` OK;
  `read_file(MISSING)` -> `Error` OK; `search_files` was the **sole MISSING slot** — fixed.
  One residual gap: `read_file` with an inverted line range silently reads to EOF -> filed as
  [rebar:4c2b-7b86-913e-40ee].

## Deferred, filed and linked `discovered_from` this ticket

* [rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e] — no loop breaker: `tool_step_limit` never set on the primary verify step
* [rebar:fd84-92b4-01ba-4911] — bounded recovery unreachable for a step-budget `LLMRunnerError`
* [rebar:8b97-a0ca-82a4-4d4e] — repetition diagnostic computed then dropped
* [rebar:218e-0ec1-385d-493a] — `--force-close` offered as the remedy for a RESOURCE exhaustion
* [rebar:4c2b-7b86-913e-40ee] — `read_file` inverted-range silent read-to-EOF
* [rebar:354d-c85d-6689-4302] — pre-existing CI red on `main`

## Replication — what this predicts for e369

Replaying **all 187 `search_files` calls the failed run actually made** against the fixed tool:

* **72** that returned `"(no matches)"` now return real hits — they were lies;
* 83 were honest absences and are unchanged; 32 already had hits and are unchanged.

The loop's decisive call is broken at the source:

    search_files("J1", "tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_characterization.py")
    before: "(no matches)"   (31 times, driving the cycle)
    after : "...:116: # J1 (rebar-ticket acb2-1823-2f0d-415b) — extraction oracles."

**Prediction, stated precisely:** this removes the *proven* cause of the non-convergence, so the
close should now RUN TO A VERDICT rather than exhaust. It does **not** predict the verdict is PASS.
Two residual risks, both outside this fix's scope: there is still no loop breaker
([rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e]), so a different loop could form; and the epic's criterion #1 ("every
child story is closed and its change is `Verified +1` on Gerrit") is not checkable from the
repository at all — the Gerrit half has no evidence any tool here can reach, and the deterministic
child-closure proof the precheck already computed is never surfaced to the verifier. That criterion
is the most likely route to a genuine FAIL.

The ticket is deliberately NOT being closed yet, because closing it may silently drop identified-but-unticketed residual scope. The RCA measured roughly 88s of deterministic pre-LLM CPU (child_closure_findings ~47.5s plus epic_bug_floor_findings ~41.0s) which CONTRADICTS the budget stated in docs/llm-framework.md around lines 680-683. No separate ticket was found covering that. Before closing bf31, either split that measurement out into its own ticket or record here that it is intentionally out of scope. Phase 2 was scoped to the search_files defect only, and the ticket framing was self-corrected as REFUTED.

compiled_state.description:
# The completion gate cannot verify a large epic: step budget exhausts at 480 AND at 1600

> **Scope note.** The title states the reported end-state. THIS ticket delivers only the
> `search_files` file-path fix — the loop's fuel and an independent signed-gate false-FAIL vector.
> Full epic-verifiability is restored jointly with the four sibling tickets linked
> `discovered_from` this one (loop breaker, recovery reachability, diagnostic sidecar,
> `--force-close` remedy).

## The failure

Closing epic [rebar:e369-a449-4773-48fb] (59 descendants, all closed and certified) fails:

    Error: cannot close e369-a449-4773-48fb: completion verification could not run
    (completion verification workflow did not produce a verdict: step 'decide@then/verify' failed:
     agent exceeded its step budget (max_iterations=480; ~1 model request per tool call).
     Raise REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS or narrow the task.)

Retried with `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=1600` (3.3x the default). **Exhausted again**, after ~50 minutes,
identical message, `max_iterations=1600`.

## MEASURED root cause (rebar-debug Phase 1 — see the RCA comment)

An instrumented reproduction (every agent tool call logged; 264 calls, 1074s, `max_iterations=480`)
settled the question by measurement: **the verifier LOOPS; it does not converge at any budget.**
Novelty by quartile: calls 1-132 are 94-98% novel, calls 199-264 are **0% novel**. From call #121
(t=537s) the agent is in a closed 4-call cycle repeated 31-37x against a single file.

The loop's engine is a tool defect: **`search_files` silently returns `"(no matches)"` when its
`path` argument names a FILE rather than a directory** (and likewise for a path that does not
exist). `src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py:109` walks `os.walk(base)`; `os.walk` on a file yields nothing,
so control falls through to `return "\n".join(hits) or "(no matches)"` at `pai_tools.py:141`. There
is no file/directory discrimination and no existence check.

Ground-truthed live in-run false negatives: `search_files("J1", ".../test_backend_characterization.py")`
-> `(no matches)` while `J1` is on line 116 of that file (this is the loop); `allow_insecure` in
`src/rebar/_config_schema.py` -> `(no matches)` with **21 real hits**; `resolved_statuses` in the same
file -> `(no matches)` with 5 real hits. Aggregate: **48% of `search_files` calls passed a file path,
100% of those returned `(no matches)`, and 26 of 29 had the literal genuinely present** — 29% of every
tool call in the run was a guaranteed-false negative.

Beyond the wasted budget this is a **false-FAIL vector on a signed gate**: the packaged
`completion-verifier` prompt tells the agent that `(no matches)` means "only that *that literal
string* is absent", and encourages narrowing the search path — the exact move that returns a lie.

## Scope of THIS ticket

This ticket fixes **only** the `search_files` path-handling defect. It is the smallest change that
removes the loop's fuel and closes the signed-gate false-FAIL vector. Four further defects were
proven in the same investigation and are filed separately (linked `discovered_from` this ticket)
because each changes gate control flow or operator messaging and deserves its own review:

* no loop breaker — `RunRequest.tool_step_limit` is never set for the primary verify step;
* the bounded completion recovery is unreachable for a step-budget `LLMRunnerError`;
* the repetition diagnostic is computed and then dropped (no `gate_error_v1` sidecar);
* the close gate offers `--force-close` as the remedy for a RESOURCE exhaustion.

`read_file`'s inverted-range fallback (`pai_tools.py:63`) is also deliberately **out of scope**: it
was not part of the proven mechanism (the inverted read actually returned text containing the sought
literal), and changing a second function's contract in this repo-wide shared module would materially
widen the review surface. Filed separately.

## The fix

In `src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py`, `search_files` must resolve its `path` argument before walking:

* `path` names an existing **file** -> scan that single file and return its `file:line: text` hits,
  applying the `_SCAN_MAX_FILES` / `_SEARCH_MAX_HITS` caps. It must **not** apply the DISCOVERY
  filter: `skip_file` (`fs_tools.py:124-127`) hides gitignored files via `_git_tracked`
  (`fs_tools.py:95-113`), and applying it to an explicitly named path would answer `"(no matches)"`
  for a file that plainly contains the literal — this bug's lie in different clothes. `read_file`
  already settled the precedent (`fs_tools.py:42-43`): "an explicitly named file is always readable
  (only the security deny-list blocks it)";
* `path` names an existing **directory** -> **unchanged** `os.walk` behaviour (every existing caller
  depends on this; the contract must not move);
* `path` does not exist -> return an explicit `Error: ...` string, never `"(no matches)"`, so an
  agent can tell "I mistyped the path" from "the literal is absent".

`"(no matches)"` must from now on mean exactly one thing: the literal was searched for and is absent.

`search_files`'s **docstring must be updated in the same change**. Pydantic AI binds plain functions
and reads their signature + docstring as the model-facing tool description (`pai_tools.py:46`), so the
docstring IS the contract the agent is given. Today it says only "search across text files under
`path`". Fixing the behaviour without the docstring would leave agents still believing a file path is
not a valid `path`, which defeats the point of the fix — the looping verifier narrowed to a file path
precisely because the packaged prompt told it to.

## Blast radius

`pai_tools.py` supplies the read-only tools to **every** LLM gate (plan-review, code-review,
completion), so the change is repo-wide in effect even though the diff is one function. The
directory-path branch is therefore held byte-identical in behaviour and is pinned by a regression
test, and the change is additive: it converts two cases that currently return a false
`"(no matches)"` into a true hit list and an explicit error respectively. No caller passes a file
path today expecting `"(no matches)"` — that value is indistinguishable from the honest-absence
answer, so nothing can be relying on it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `search_files(query, path)` where `path` names an existing FILE that contains `query` returns
      the `file:line: text` hit(s), not `"(no matches)"`
- [x] `search_files(query, path)` where `path` names an existing FILE that does NOT contain `query`
      still returns `"(no matches)"` (honest absence is preserved)
- [x] `search_files(query, path)` where `path` names a DIRECTORY is unchanged — same hits, same
      ordering, same caps (regression pin; every existing gate depends on it)
- [x] `search_files(query, path)` where `path` does not exist returns an explicit `Error: ...`,
      never `"(no matches)"`
- [x] a **gitignored** file named explicitly as `path`, which contains `query`, returns its hits —
      the discovery filter must not hide a file the caller named (pinned with a git fixture that
      asserts the filter is genuinely armed before trusting the result)
- [x] the repo-root confinement and deny-list of `_safe_path` still apply to a file path — a file
      outside the root or on the deny-list is refused exactly as a directory is
- [x] `search_files`'s docstring states that `path` may name a file (scanned as one file) or a
      directory (walked), and that an unsearchable path returns `Error: ...` — the docstring is the
      model-facing tool contract Pydantic AI passes to the agent (`pai_tools.py:46`)
- [x] the RED test is shown failing for the right reason before the fix exists, and passing after
